question.text: The chapter cites the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) definition of a 'start-up' for Indian VC financing. A business qualifies as a start-up if it is not more than ____ years old and has NOT recorded a turnover of more than INR ____ crore in any financial year.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The chapter explicitly states: 'the Government of India under DPIIT defines a start-up as a business that is not more than 10 years old and has not recorded a turnover of more than INR 100 crore in any financial year.' These are the two cumulative tests; the entity must also be engaged in innovation or a scalable business model. **The Trap:** (A), (C), (D) are all outdated or fabricated thresholds. The DPIIT thresholds were revised UPWARD to 10 years and INR 100 crore (from earlier 7 years / INR 25 crore) to widen the start-up tax-incentive net. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C also cites the same DPIIT definition. Income Tax 80-IAC exemption questions on other exams (e.g., taxation papers) cross-reference it. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When a Cat I VCF's investee claims DPIIT start-up status for the Section 54GB / 80-IAC tax incentives, insist on a valid DPIIT recognition certificate and annual turnover certificate. Losing start-up status mid-holding can upset the investee's ESOP taxation and the fund's Section 10(23FB) pass-through chain.
